checks.name: identity
checks.reason: Subject reads as the requested plush toy panda with black eye patches and a small green shoulder dragon companion. The delivered portrait and native/exported multiviews consistently show the same panda/dragon pairing and proportions (large head, compact toy body) without added props/clothing/scenery.

checks.name: appearance
checks.reason: Native render matches the intended plush look: soft, short groomed fur with clean black/ivory boundaries, expressive eyes with catchlights, and a distinct green dragon with visible sculpted details (spines/wings/tail) that is not covered in panda fur.

checks.name: appearance
checks.reason: Exported representation does not match the requested “soft, neatly groomed short fur” look: it shows conspicuous sparse/spiky card-like tufts and patchy coverage over the panda (notably on head/body), producing a rough, stubbly silhouette and visible flecking rather than a continuous plush undercoat. These artifacts are prominent in exported multiview and during motion, making the exported avatar read lower-quality/less plush than native.

checks.name: framing
checks.reason: Full character (panda + perched dragon) is visible in front/side/back/three-quarter views for both native and exported. No extra props/clothing/text/pedestal/scenery are present.

limitations: Motion evidence is a contact-sheet style sampling; it does not prove continuous-time collisions, ground contact, balance, or seamless looping across all frames (even if endpoints match).
Only one isolated ‘greatest_recorded_edge_stretch’ pose is provided per representation; localized deformation/clipping elsewhere in the clip could be missed.
required_repairs: Fix exported fur/portable coat appearance to match the intended plush short-fur look: eliminate the obvious sparse spiky card tips and patchy coverage (especially on the panda head and torso). Target a denser, more even short pile with a cleaner silhouette and fewer visible individual card protrusions in exported views and during motion.
Re-check exported motion appearance after fur fix to ensure the panda surface does not show conspicuous bald flecks/patches or harsh card artifacts during the dance frames.

state_reviews.reason: The clip shows real pose changes (sways/leans and some arm/head articulation). However, the requested “small whole-body hops” are not clearly readable as hops from the provided motion contact sheet; the feet appear largely planted with no obvious up/down hop moments visible at the sampled frames. Additionally, exported fur artifacts are prominent during the motion, harming the intended plush presentation even when the motion itself changes.

requirement_reviews.reason: Across the sampled frames, the panda alternates side-to-side leaning/weight shifts multiple times over the 4 seconds, reading as repeated beats rather than a single sway.

Side-to-side sways are visible, but the ‘small whole-body hops’ are not clearly readable as hops in the provided sampled frames; the motion looks primarily like leaning/swaying with minimal apparent vertical lift.
Both arms change pose in coordination with the side-to-side beats (hands/forearms shift position across the sampled times), reading as toy-like arm swinging rather than remaining static.
Head/neck orientation changes are visible across the sampled frames (gentle tilts accompanying the sways).
The green dragon remains perched on the shoulder throughout the sampled frames with no visible separation, flight, or drifting away; it follows the panda’s body movement.
The final sampled frame visually matches the starting overall pose closely (body returns to the initial stance/orientation).
Arms appear to return to their starting relaxed position by the end frame rather than holding a final gesture.
Head appears to return near-neutral at the end, matching the starting orientation closely.

raw_answer.summary: Native appearance meets the plush panda + perched green dragon brief, but exported fur/portable coat renders with conspicuous spiky/sparse card artifacts and patchiness that break the requested soft, neatly groomed short-fur look. The toy dance shows readable sways/tilts and returns to start, but the required ‘small whole-body hops’ are not clearly readable from the provided motion evidence. Requires repair before acceptance.

plan.generation_prompt: Create a single plush toy panda avatar with a small green dragon companion perched on its shoulder, matching the provided reference portrait. Panda: rounded plush proportions, large head, short muzzle, black eye patches, black ears/arms/legs, ivory/white face and belly; soft neatly groomed short fur as a continuous undercoat surface (no coarse carved fur spikes). Clean, tidy color boundaries. Dragon: small green dragon sitting/perched on the panda shoulder, kept distinct from panda fur; preserve visible surface details (spines, tail, small wings) with a matte, slightly textured reptile-like finish. Materials: panda fur soft/matte with subtle sheen; eyes glossy with clear highlights; nose slightly glossy; dragon skin/scales matte-satin; avoid overall shiny plastic. Pose: neutral, animation/
limitations: Dance/hops are authored keyframed motion only; no physical balance, foot-ground contact solving, or impact dynamics are implied.
Keeping the dragon perched is treated as a rigid attachment to the shoulder region during animation; no independent dragon flight or separation is authored in this run.
Exact one-to-one reconstruction of the reference image geometry is not guaranteed; the prompt specifies intended appearance for generation/texture.
plan.reason: Planned one custom 4-second toy dance state with rhythmic side-to-side beats, small whole-body hops, coordinated arm swings, gentle head tilts, and a return to the starting pose while keeping the shoulder dragon attached; no unsupported interaction/expression features requested.

states.meaning: Cheerful 4-second toy dance: three alternating side-to-side beats with small whole-body hops, coordinated arm swings, gentle head tilts; the shoulder dragon stays perched/attached; ends in the starting pose.

requirements.description: Perform three clearly readable alternating side-to-side beats over the clip duration (left-right-left or right-left-right), with timing that reads as an intentional rhythm.
Add small whole-body hops synchronized with the beat: visible upward-and-downward body motion (toy-like, modest amplitude) while also shifting side-to-side.
Swing both arms in coordination with the side-to-side beats (arms move visibly and symmetrically/alternating in a toy-dance style; no new props).
Gently tilt the head in coordination with the beat (small, readable tilts; maintain a friendly toy demeanor).
Keep the dragon perched and attached to the panda shoulder throughout: the dragon follows the shoulder/body motion without separating, flying, or drifting away.
Finish in the same overall starting pose: panda body position/orientation returns to its initial placement at the end of the clip.
Finish with arms returning to their starting pose (no held-out final gesture).
Finish with head returning to its starting pose (neutral at clip end).

roles.description: Main panda body/root including torso, hips/legs and overall translation used for sways and small hops.
Both panda arms/forearms/paws used for coordinated swinging.
Panda head/neck used for gentle tilts (no facial expression requirements).
Green shoulder dragon companion attached on the panda shoulder; must remain perched and follow along.

states.user_request: A cheerful four-second toy dance with three alternating side-to-side beats, small whole-body hops, coordinated arm swings and gentle head tilts. Keep the shoulder dragon perched. previous_answer.reason: Continuation reuses the prior authored rig, bindings, and toy_dance keys. Repairs are limited to measured failures: (1) severe deformation outliers from belly/hip vertices carrying left-arm influences—tightened weight_constraints arm regions to keep arm weights confined to the actual arm volumes and clamp stray arm weights from the far-left belly area back to torso (fallback chest); (2) native finishing failures from surface_profiles reporting face-count bounds violations—relaxed min/max face guards for nose_satin and dragon_matte_satin and slightly tightened their ellipsoid regions to better localize selection while preserving the intended matte/satin looks.
